title: Perinatal taurine supplementation influences renal hemodynamics and excretory function in adult, female rats

sections.abstract: <jats:p>Perinatal taurine supplementation and depletion influences cardiovascular and renal function in adult, male rats. This study further investigates the effect of perinatal taurine status on renal function in adult conscious, female rats. Female Sprague‐Dawley rats were fed normal rat chow with 3% beta‐alanine (taurine depletion, TD), 3% taurine (taurine supplementation, TS) or water alone (Control, C) from conception to weaning. Female offspring were then fed with the normal rat chow and tap water ad libitum. At 7–8 weeks of age, their hemodynamic parameters and renal function were studied in a conscious, restrained state. Body, heart, and kidney weights were not significantly different among groups. Mean arterial pressures but not heart rates had a tendency to be higher in TD compared to C and TS rats. Basal plasma sodium and potassium, hematocrit, fasting and non‐fasting blood glucose, and glucose tolerance were all within normal limits. While diuretic responses to an acute saline load (5% body weight) were similar among groups, their natriuretic responses had a tendency to be higher in TS rats. Fractional sodium but not water excretion was significantly higher in TS compared to C and TD groups. Glomerular filtration rates and filtration fraction were not significantly different among the three groups while effective renal blood flows were significantly lower in TS rats. A sharp rise in resting renovascular resistance and its rapid fall responses to isotonic saline load were also observed in the TS animals. The present data suggest that perinatal tuarine status also has long‐term effects on renal hemodynamics and excretory function in female rats.</jats:p>
